answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 23% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the lagoon balance is debited each close, the dawn ledger makes public the bleed, and the velvet audit lists every fee. An operator holding 284 idle keys therefore pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
